Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance
Bodily Injury Unit
Claim Notes
Claim number:
C-1053
Claimant:
Mary Warren
Adjuster:
Darin Tyler
August 12, 2025
The claimant reported a low-speed collision in a parking lot and stated they felt neck pain within the hour, and the file
was opened for a bodily injury and property damage review.
August 26, 2025
Photos taken at the scene show damage to the rear bumper and tail lamp assembly, and the vehicle daamge
matches the impact described by the claimant.
September 23, 2025
The police report confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the collision, and the responding officer's
notes match the location and sequence given.
October 22, 2025
No independent witnesses have come forward, so the file relies on scene photos, the police report, and the claimant's
own statements.
November 11, 2025
The claimant was reached by phone and gave the same account of how the collision happened as in the initial report,
with no changes in the sequence or the parties involved.
December 10, 2025
The driver is named on the policy and the coverage was active on the date of loss, and nothing in the records
suggests the vehicle damage predates the policy start.
December 19, 2025
A check of the vehicle's prior claims and repair history shows no earlier damage to the same areas of the vehicle.
January 28, 2026
The claimant's medical records show a diagnosis of whiplash consistent with the kind and force of a rear-end impact,
and the treatment plan followed a typical course of care.
February 25, 2026
Records also show no prior neck or upper back complaints or treatment, and no earlier injury to the same body area
is known.
March 13, 2026
Follow-up ntoes show the claimant's symptoms improved steadily, and the frequecny of visits tapered as recovery
progressed.
March 19, 2026
Based on the medical records, vehicle damage, and police report, the claim is consistent with the reported loss and
the file is moving toward a settlement evaluation.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- occurrence_support: Do independent sources (witnesses, photos, cameras, the other driver) confirm that the accident happened as described? Allowed: Confirmed, Partially corroborated, Uncorroborated, Contradicted, Suspected staged.
- damage_crash_fit: Does the vehicle damage fit the described impact? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- account_stability: Did the claimant's account of the accident stay the same over time? Allowed: Stable, Clarified, Materially changed.
- occupant_presence: Was the claimant really in the vehicle at the time of the crash? Allowed: Verified, Unclear, Added later, Not present.
- prior_damage_evidence: Is there evidence of vehicle damage from before this crash? Allowed: None, Possible, Documented, Material.
- known_loss_evidence: Is there evidence the damage existed or was known before the coverage started? Allowed: Weak, Moderate, Strong.
- driver_status: Is the driver of the insured vehicle on the policy? Allowed: Listed, Household, Unlisted, Excluded.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
